record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: Can numerical and analytic methods be extended to obtain general stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov-Maxwell solutions with charged massive Vlasov particles interacting through the electromagnetic field, beyond perturbative regimes where total angular momentum and gravitational-field strength remain restricted?

evidence.quote: Another interesting direction of research, and possible extension of the code [6], is the addition of charge.
Allowing the particles to be charged (in addition to having mass) and interact additionally through the electromagnetic field leads to the Einstein-Vlasov-Maxwell system.

The total angular momentum and the strength of the gravitational field are still restricted, and an understanding of general solutions to the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov-Maxwell system is lacking.

artifact.status_search_result: Existence results for stationary axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov–Maxwell solutions have been obtained only via perturbative/implicit function theorem arguments around known backgrounds, in which the total angular momentum and gravitational-field strength remain restricted. A general (non-perturbative) understanding of axially symmetric charged Vlasov solutions remains lacking, and the problem appears to be open as of recent surveys and research.

status_evidence.title: Rotating Clouds of Charged Vlasov Matter in General Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of stationary axially symmetric (non-spherical) solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov–Maxwell system established via the implicit function theorem on Banach spaces, in a perturbative regime.
status_evidence.claim: Only perturbative existence results are available; no general non-perturbative theory yet.

status_evidence.title: The Einstein-Vlasov System/Kinetic Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Survey indicating that most rigorous work on Einstein–Vlasov–Maxwell concerns spherical symmetry, with axially symmetric results being recent and restricted.
status_evidence.claim: General axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov–Maxwell solutions are not yet understood.
